s: Which continent has the largest number of people living in poverty
The World's largest continent by area?
x: Asia is the largest continent, with about 44.57 million sq km, or 29.8% of the world's land. 'America' is not a single continent in this list.

s: Which one of the following is the continent with the highest mean elevation in the world?
x: Antarctica is the highest continent on Earth, with an average elevation of approximately 2,300 to 2,500 meters (about 7,500–8,200 feet). This extreme elevation is primarily due to the massive, thick ice sheet covering over 98% of the landmass, which averages over 2,000 meters in thickness.

s: Which of the following presents the correct sequence (in descending order) of the area of the continents?
x: Asia – 44,568,500 sq. km Africa – 30,065,000 sq. km North America – 24,473,000 sq. km Europe – 9,948,000 sq. km

s: Which one of the following is smallest Continent ?
x: Asia – 44,568,500 sq. km Africa – 30,065,000 sq. km North America – 24,473,000 sq. km Europe – 9,948,000 sq. km

s: The satellites of which one of the following countries have helped in the preparation of a detailed and complete map of Antarctica?
x: RADARSAT-1, the satellite of Canada which helped in the preparation of a detailed and complete map of Antarctica for the first time in 1997.

s: Taylor Valley is located in –
x: Taylor Valley which is located in Antarctica was discovered by Robert Falcon Scott in 1903. He gave it the name ‘’Valley of the Dead’’.

s: Congo is situated in –
x: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is located in Africa. Democratic Republic of the Congo is situated at the Equator. It is the second largest country in Africa after Algeria. Republic of Congo is also a country in Africa and Equator passes through it.

s: Which one of the following is the continent with the highest mean elevation in the world?
x: Antarctica is the continent with the highest mean elevation in the world. It is situated around the South Pole. Average elevation of continents is as follows: Antarctica - 2300 meters Africa - 585 meters North America - 760 meters South America - 554 meters Asia - 923 meters Europe - 302 meters Australia - 330 meters

s: Which one of the following Continents has the highest percentage of plains in its total area ?
x: Plains largely constitute Europe and South America however in terms of percentage Europe has the largest percentage of plains compared to its total area.

s: Which one the following is the correct sequence of the given continents in the descending order of their percentage of Earth's land?
x: According to Phillip’s Atlas, the percentage of the land area of the continent in respect of their total land area of the Earth is as follows – Asia - 29.8% Africa - 20.3% North America - 16.2% South America - 11.8% Antarctica - 9.2% Europe - 6.8% Australia - 5.9% Thus the descending order of continents given in the question in respect of their land area percentage is Africa – North America – South America – Europe.

s: Which one of the following continents has the largest number of countries?
x: The number of countries in the following continents is as follows : Africa 54 Europe 49 Asia 48 North America 23 Oceania 14 South America 12 2. Among the following continents, which one has the highest number of countries? (a) Europe (b) Asia (c) Africa (d) North America (e) None of the above/More than one of the above 66th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2020 Ans. (c) See the explanation of the above question.

s: Which of the following continents has the maximum per capita land ?
x: According to "World Bank data, the Australian continent has the maximum per capita land.

s: The two smallest Continents of the world are –
x: Asia – 44,568,500 sq. km Africa – 30,065,000 sq. km North America – 24,473,000 sq. km Europe – 9,948,000 sq. km

s:
From the code given below select the correct sequence of the following continents in terms of their area in descending order:
(1) Europe
(2) Australia
(3) Africa
(4) South America
x: Guyana is a country located in the continent of South America. Therefore Guyana is not located in the continent of Africa. The capital of Guyana is George Town. Gabon lies along the Atlantic coast of Central Africa. Guinea is in West Africa, bordered on the west by the Atlantic Ocean. Guinea - Bissau is a tropical country on West Africa's Atlantic coast.

s: As per area which of the following is the largest continent?
x: There are a total of 7 continents in the world- Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia. Asia is the largest continent having an area of 44,568,500 sq. km. The area of other continents is as follows– Africa - 30,065,000 sq. km. North America - 24,473,000 sq. km. South America - 17,819,000 sq. km. Antarctica - 14,200,000 sq. km Europe - 9,948,000 sq. km. Australia - 7,741,220 sq. km.

s: The geographical area of Asia is
x: Asia's area is about 44,568,500 sq km, i.e. roughly 44 million sq km, so option 4 is correct.

s: ‘Dakshin Gangotri’ is situated in …… .
x: Dakshin Gangotri was India's first Antarctic research station, set up in 1983-84 on the Antarctic ice shelf. It is not in Uttarakhand, the Himalayas or the Arctic.

s: Arrange the following continents in descending order according to their landmass percentage?
o: North America, Africa, South America, Europe
Africa, North America, South America, Europe
x: By share of land, Africa (20.3%) > North America (16.2%) > South America (11.8%) > Europe (6.8%). That matches option 2. The other options put North America first or leave out South America.

s: Which one of the following continent is considered as ‘Cradle of Mankind’?
x: Africa is called the 'Cradle of Mankind' because the earliest human fossils and ancestors have been found there, for example in East Africa and South Africa.

s: Which is the biggest continent in the world on which world’s highest population is found?
x: Asia is the largest continent by area (44.57 million sq km, 29.8% of land) and also the most populous.

s: Mexico is situated in
x: Mexico lies in North America, south of the USA. The notes do not state this directly, so no line is linked.

s: Brazil is situated in which continent?
x: Brazil is the largest country of South America, which is the continent in which it lies, not Europe, North America or Africa.

s: Which of the following is not included in the geographical group of countries designated the name Oceania?
x: Oceania covers Australia, Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia. Indonesia is generally treated as part of Asia (Southeast Asia), so it is the odd one out.

s: Which among the following continent is biggest according to their sizes?
x: By area the order is Africa > North America > South America > Europe, so Africa is the biggest of the options.

s: Name the continent which is nearest to the Antarctica.
x: South America is the continent closest to Antarctica, across the Drake Passage. Africa, Australia and Asia are farther away.

s: Which continent is also known as Continent of Bird?
x: South America is called the 'Continent of Birds' because of its great bird diversity, with the most bird species of any continent.

s:
Arrange the following continents in decreasing order according to their sizes

I. Europe
II. Australia

III. Africa
IV. South America
Codes
x: The descending order of area is Africa > South America > Europe > Australia, which is III, IV, I, II.

s: The 3rd Indian Research Centre had been founded in Antarctica by the name of :
x: The 3rd research centre in Antarctica was established in 2012 with the name of Bharati.

s: Which continent ranks third in the world by area?
x: The order is Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

s: How many countries does Africa have?
x: Africa has 54 countries, the most of any continent; Asia has 48 and Europe 49.

s: What is the mean elevation of Antarctica?
x: Antarctica's ice sheet gives it the highest mean elevation, about 2,300 m; Asia's is 923 m and North America's 760 m.

s: Which of the following was NOT a part of Gondwana?
x: Gondwana included Antarctica, South America, Africa, Australia, Arabia and Peninsular India, but not North America.

s: Which continent has the highest percentage of plains?
x: Europe has the highest share of plains among the continents.

s: Which satellite produced the first detailed and complete map of Antarctica in 1997?
x: Canada's RADARSAT-1 made the first detailed, complete map of Antarctica in 1997.

Consider the following countries:
I. Chile
II. Venezuela
III. Ecuador
IV. Peru
V. Colombia
Which of the above South American countries have a Pacific coastline?
x: Several South American countries have coastlines along the Pacific Ocean. These include Chile, Ecuador, Peru and Colombia. Venezuela lies along the Caribbean Sea rather than the Pacific Ocean.

s: Which of the following groups of countries is arranged in descending order of area?
x: The correct descending order of countries by area is: Russia '! Canada "! United States '! China. Russia is the largest country in the world by land area.

s: Which country in the world has the longest coastline?
x: Canada Canada, with its vast Arctic archipelago and extensive Atlantic and Pacific coasts, has the longest coastline of any country in the world.

s: Which of the following became the world's first country to make abortion a constitutional right?
x: France became the first country to explicitly protect abortion as a constitutional right, when it amended its constitution in March 2024.

s: The capital of the Congo is
x: Brazzaville is the capital of the Republic of the Congo.

s: The capital of the Congo is
x: Brazzaville is the capital of the Republic of the Congo.

s: Israel has a common border with —
o: Jordan, Syria, Iraq and Saudi Arabia
x: Israel shares borders with Lebanon (north), Syria (northeast), Jordan (east) and Egypt (southwest).

s: Which of the following countries has common borders with the largest number of countries?
x: Russia shares land borders with more countries than any other nation (14 as commonly cited), owing to its vast size spanning two continents.

s: Which one of the following countries is landlocked?
x: Bolivia is a landlocked country in South America, meaning it has no direct access to the sea. Peru, Suriname, and Uruguay all have coastlines.

s: The longest border between any two countries in the world is between:
o: Canada and the United States of America
x: The International Boundary between Canada and the USA is the longest international border in the world, with around 8,891 kilometres from the Pacific Ocean in the west to the Atlantic Ocean in the east. The Russia-Kazakhstan Border holds the distinction of being the longest continuous international border globally and ranks as the second longest in total length, following the Canada-United States border.

s: Which one of the following countries is land-locked?
x: Bolivia is a land-locked country in South America. 6. Which one of the following continents has no landlocked country? (a) Africa (b) Asia (c) Europe (d) North America U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2005 Ans. (d) There is no landlocked country in the North American continent. The United States of America, Canada and Mexico etc. have sea coastlines

s: Alaska is a part of –
x: Alaska is a province of United State of America situated in the northwest extremity. The United State purchased Alaska from the Russian Empire on March 30, 1867. Significantly, the treaty was signed by President Andrew Johnson on May 28, 1867 and Alaska was formally transferred to the US on 18 Oct. 1867.

s: Where does India rank in the area among the countries of the world?
x: India is the seventh largest country after Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil and Australia respectively by area and the first largest (state of the World Population report, 2023) by population. It occupies about 2.4 percent of the total area of the land surface. The mainland of India extends between 8º4' North to 37º6' North latitudes, while the tropical zone is stretched between 23º 30' North and South latitudes. Therefore statements 1 and 3 is incorrect. The latitudinal extension of the whole of India (including Andaman & Nicobar Islands) lies between 6º45' to 37º 6' North latitudes. 82º 30' East longitude is used to determine Indian Standard Time.

s: The longest border between any two countries in the world is between:
o: Canada and the United States of America
x: Canada's border with the United States of America is the world's longest international border, at 8,891 km. In comparison, the border between the Russian Federation and Kazakhstan measures 6,846 km. and the Chile-Argentina border measures 5,308 km. while India shares 3,488 km. of border with China. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

s: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
x: The correct match of countries and their capitals is as follows: Ghana - Accra Kenya - Nairobi Namibia - Windhoek Nigeria - Abuja Thus (d) is not correctly matched.

s: The largest country in the world is :
x: The correct order of countries in descending order of their area is as follows - Canada, U.S.A., China and Brazil.

s: Which of the following countries is not larger than India in terms of Area?
x: India is the seventh largest country in the world in terms of area. In this context, the six countries larger than India are- Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil and Australia. Thus, France is not larger than India.

s: India is in size -
o: Fifth largest country in the world
Sixth largest country in the world
Seventh largest country in the world
x: India is the seventh largest country after Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil and Australia respectively by area and the first largest (state of the World Population report, 2023) by population. It occupies about 2.4 percent of the total area of the land surface. The mainland of India extends between 8º4' North to 37º6' North latitudes, while the tropical zone is stretched between 23º 30' North and South latitudes. Therefore statements 1 and 3 is incorrect. The latitudinal extension of the whole of India (including Andaman & Nicobar Islands) lies between 6º45' to 37º 6' North latitudes. 82º 30' East longitude is used to determine Indian Standard Time.

s: Durban city is situated in –
x: Tasmania is an island state of Australia. It is separated by Bass Strait. Thus (a) is not correctly matched. Sicily is the largest of the Italian islands, situated in the Mediterranean Sea. The total area of the island is 25,711 sq. km. Newfoundland is situated in the eastern part of Canada. It is often described as the mid point of Atlantic Ocean. Durban is the third largest town of South Africa in terms of population. It is also famous as the busiest port in South Africa.

s: Which country has the largest coastline?
x: The longest coastline in the world is of Canada with (202,080 km) followed by Norway (83281 km.) Indonesia (54,716 km), Greenland (Part fo the Realm of Denmark) (44,087 km), Russia (37,653 km) and Philippines (36,289 km).

s: The correct ascending order of the following countries in terms of area is :
x: The correct sequence of the countries in ascending order of their area is as follows- Country Total Area (in sq. km) Argentina - 2796427 India - 3287263 Australia - 7692024 Brazil - 8510417 4. The river situated along the border between the United States of America and Mexico is : (a) The Mississippi (b) The Colorado (c) The Rio Grande (d) The Amazon U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023 Ans. (b) & (c) The Rio Grande and Colorado rivers are situated along the border between the United States of America and Mexico. The United States and Mexico share the waters of the Colorado River and the Rio Grande. A bilateral water treaty from 1944 (the 1944 Water Treaty) and other binational agreements guide how the two governments share the flows of these rivers. The binational International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC) administers these agreements.

s: Which one of the following countries has the longest coastline?
x: The longest coastline in the world is of Canada with (202,080 km) followed by Norway (83281 km.) Indonesia (54,716 km), Greenland (Part fo the Realm of Denmark) (44,087 km), Russia (37,653 km) and Philippines (36,289 km).

s: Marx belonged to
x: Karl Marx was born in Trier, Prussia (Germany), so Germany is correct; he later lived in France and Britain but belonged to Germany.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched? Countries Cities
x: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus. The other pairs are wrong: Bogota is Colombia's capital, Caracas is Venezuela's, and Wellington is New Zealand's.

s: Which among the following countries is not located in Africa?
x: Guyana is in northern South America, while Gabon, Guinea and Guinea-Bissau are all African countries.

s: The African Country, Ghana was earlier known as
x: Ghana was called the Gold Coast under British rule and became independent in 1957 as Ghana. Tanganyika is the former name of mainland Tanzania.

s:
Consider the following pairs. Regions Sometimes Countries Mentioned in News

I. Catalonia – Spain

II. Crimea – Hungary

III. Mindanao – Philippines

IV. Oromia – Nigeria
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Catalonia is a region of Spain and Mindanao is in the Philippines. Crimea is tied to Ukraine/Russia, not Hungary, and Oromia is in Ethiopia, not Nigeria.

s: Which among the following group of countries are also called as Benelux countries?
x: Benelux is the economic union of Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg, whose names form the acronym.

s: Alaska is the part of which of the following countries?
Which one of the following is a land locked country in Africa?
x: Chad is a landlocked country in Africa. Angola, Kenya and Senegal all have coastlines.

s: Which one of the following countries is called the ‘country of winds’?
x: Denmark is known as the country of winds because of its extensive wind energy and windy climate.

s: The group of countries consisting of Norway, Swedan, Iceland, Denmark and Finland is called as
x: Norway, Sweden, Iceland, Denmark and Finland together are known as the Nordic countries.

s: Which country is also known as the ‘Land of Rising Sun’?
x: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun, as its name Nippon means 'origin of the sun'.

s: The capital of Peru is
x: Lima is the capital of Peru; the notes do not state this, but Lisbon (Portugal) and Madrid (Spain) are European capitals.

s: Which one of the following countries does not border with Lithuania?
x: Lithuania borders Poland, Belarus, Latvia and Russia's Kaliningrad, but not Ukraine.

s: Which one of the following pairs (Country and Capitals) is not properly matched?
x: Tokyo, not Kyoto, is the capital of Japan, so the Japan–Kyoto pair is wrong.

s: Helsinki is the capital of
x: Helsinki is the capital of Finland; Denmark, Norway and Sweden have Copenhagen, Oslo and Stockholm.

s: Which among the following is known as Land of Morning Calm?
x: Korea is traditionally called the Land of the Morning Calm; Japan is the Land of the Rising Sun.

s: Vienna is the capital of which country?
x: Vienna is the capital of Austria, not of Australia, whose capital is Canberra.

s: Zimbabwe was earlier known as
x: Zimbabwe was formerly Southern Rhodesia. Gold Coast was Ghana and Belgian Congo was the Democratic Republic of Congo.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Great Britain comprises England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Island.

II. England covers less than 60% of the total area of the United Kingdom.
Which of these statements given above is/are correct?
x: Great Britain comprises England, Wales and Scotland only, not Northern Ireland, so I is wrong. England is about 130,000 of 243,000 sq km, roughly 54%, under 60%, so II is correct.

s: Which one of the following pairs (Nations and Capitals) is not correctly matched?
x: Seoul is the capital of South Korea; North Korea's capital is Pyongyang.

s: The biggest country of the world in geographical extent is
x: Russia is the largest country by area, ahead of Canada, the USA and China.

s: Which of the following cities is the seat of Parliament of South Africa?
x: South Africa's legislative capital, where Parliament sits, is Cape Town. Pretoria is the executive capital.

s:
Consider the following statements. Cities sometimes in News – Countries

I. Aleppo – Syria

II. Kirkuk – Yemen

III. Mosul – Palestine

IV. Mazar-e-Sharif – Afghanistan
Which of these is correctly matched?
x: Aleppo is in Syria and Mazar-e-Sharif is in Afghanistan. Kirkuk and Mosul are in Iraq, so II and III are wrong.

s: Which one of the following countries is not situated in North America?
x: Sierra Leone is in West Africa. Panama, Honduras and Guatemala are in Central America, part of North America.

s: Which of the following pairs are not correctly matched?
x: Malé is the capital of the Maldives. Malabo is the capital of Equatorial Guinea, so this pair is wrong.

s: Which one of the following countries is the largest country without borders in terms of geographical area?
x: Japan is an island country with no land borders and is larger than New Zealand, the Philippines and Cuba.

s: Which one of the following is not a correct match?
x: Ethiopia's capital is Addis Ababa. Lusaka is the capital of Zambia.

s: Which one of the following is not a Balkan country?
x: The Balkan region is a specific cultural region of South eastern Europe which is located near Balkan mountains. The main countries of this region are- Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Greece, Croatia, Serbia, Slovenia, Romania etc. while Austria is not related to Balkan States.

s: Zambia does not have a common border with –
x: The countries having boundaries with the Adriatic Sea are- Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Albania. Apart from these, the boundary of Italy is also connected to the Adriatic Sea. Serbia and North Macedonia are landlocked countries. Thus, option (b) is the correct answer.

s: What is Siam presently called?
x: Siam is the former name of Thailand, changed officially in 1939 and again in 1949.

s: Other than India and China, which of the following groups of countries share a land border with Myanmar?
x: Myanmar is bordered by India and Bangladesh to the northwest, China to the northeast, Laos and Thailand to the east and southeast, and the Andaman Sea and the Bay of Bengal to the south and southwest.

s: Other than India and China, which one of the following groups of countries border with Myanmar?
x: Myanmar, formerly known as Burma with a total area of 676,578 sq. km is situated in Southeast Asia. Its total border is 6522 km long. Bangladesh (271 km), China (2129 km), India (1468 km), Laos (238 km) and Thailand (2416 km) are its bordering countries. Its marine border extends to the Andaman Sea and the Bay of Bengal.

s: Which of the following countries in Asia is not a landlocked country?
x: Thailand is not a landlocked country. A landlocked country is an independent sovereign state that does not have direct access to an ocean. Some of the landlocked countries in Asia are- Afghanistan, Armenia, Bhutan, Nepal, Mongolia, etc.

s: Which city of Turkey is known as the `Gateway to the West' ?
x: Istanbul is located in the peninsular area of Turkiye whose three sides are surrounded by the Marmara Sea, Bosporus Straits and Golden Horn. It is also known as the Gateway to the West'.

s:
Consider the following countries:
1. Bulgaria
2. Czech Republic
3. Hungary
4. Latvia
5. Lithuania
6. Romania
How many of the above-mentioned countries share a land border with Ukraine?
x: Ukraine shares a border with Belarus to the north, Russia to the east, the Sea of Azov & Black Sea to the south, Moldova & Romania to the southwest and Hungary, Slovakia & Poland to the west. The capital is Kyiv (Kiev), located on the Dnieper River. The most notable rivers of Ukraine include the Dnieper, Dniester, Southern Buh & Siversky Donets. Most of the rivers of Ukraine drain into the Black Sea & Azov Sea, which belong to the larger Mediterranean basin (flow in a southerly direction). Important Cities: Kyiv, Kharkiv, Odesa, Donbas Region, Mykolaiv, Mariupol, Simferopol, etc.

s: The only land-locked Country in Southeast Asia is-
x: Laos is the only land-locked country in southeast Asia bordered by Myanmar, China, Vietnam, Cambodia and Thailand.

s:
Which of the following Countries is a land-locked country?
1. Afghanistan
2. Hungary
3. Malaysia
4. Switzerland
Choose the correct answer from the codes given below-
x: Afghanistan located in Asia is a landlocked country that borders Iran, Pakistan, India (Ladakh), China, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. Hungary is another landlocked country that borders Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Ukraine and Slovak Republic. The border of Switzerland is surrounded by France, Italy, Austria, Liechtenstein and Germany. Thus, all the above three countries have no coastline while the border of Malaysia is connected with Thailand, Indonesia, Brunei and it also has an extensive coastline. Thus, option (d) is the correct answer.

s: Which one of the following is a landlocked country?
x: A landlocked country has no access to any sea or ocean Belgium, Romania and Ukraine have coastlines. Hungary is completely surrounded by land and has no coastline. Therefore Hungary is the only landlocked country among the options. 13. Which of the following countries are landlocked?

s: Which one of the following is not a landlocked country?
x: Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan are fully landlocked countries while the north-western border of Uzbekistan stretches to the Aral Sea. Similarly, Baku the capital of Azerbaijan is located on the western shore of the Caspian Sea. So in context of this question, two of the above-mentioned options (a) and (d) seem to be correct. Aral Sea used to be a part of the former Soviet Union. The Soviet Union diverted rivers flowing into Aral Sea for various irrigation projects, as a result, it has mostly dried up and only 10% of its area is left. Caspian Sea is the world’s largest lake or sea, surrounded by land. Thus, the most appropriate answer according to the given facts should be option (d). 11. Maginot Line exists between which countries? (a) U.S.A. & Canada (b) France & Germany (c) Namibia and Angola (d) South Korea & North Korea 71st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2025 Ans. (b) The Maginot Line was a massive line of fortifications built by France before the Second World War to stop a possible attack Germany. It was mainly a fixed defensive line built on France’s eastern border facing Germany (and partly towards Luxembourg).

s: Which one of the following does not border Panama?
x: Panama shares land borders with Costa Rica (west) and Colombia (east). It is an isthmus with the Caribbean Sea to the north and the Pacific Ocean to the south, giving it long coastlines but just those two land neighbours. Venezuela does not border Panama; it lies across the Caribbean, separated by Colombia.

s: Indonesia does not share its land boundary with which one of the following countries?
x: In the given options Indonesia does not share a land boundary with Brunei. Significantly Indonesia shares borders with Malaysia on Borneo and Sebatic Island, with Papua New Guinea on New Guinea Island and with (Timor-Leste) (East Timor) on Timor Island.

s: Which of the following countries is not located in Central America?
x: Sierra Leone is a country in West Africa bordered by Guinea to the north, Liberia to the southeast and the Atlantic Ocean on West and southwest. Whereas Panama, Honduras and Guatemala are located in Central America.

s:
Consider the following countries:
1. Azerbaijan
2. Kyrgyzstan
3. Tajikistan
4. Turkmenistan
5. Uzbekistan
Which of the above has borders with Afghanistan?
x: Afghanistan is a landlocked country bounded by: East and south by Pakistan, and a 106 km border length with India; west by Iran; north by Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan; and it also has a short border with Xinjiang, China, at the end of the Wakhan Corridor.

s:
Consider the following countries :
1. Azerbaijan
2. Kyrgyzstan
3. Tajikistan
4. Turkmenistan
5. Uzbekistan
Which of the above have borders with Afghanistan?
x: Afghanistan shares borders with Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, China, India, Pakistan and Iran. So it is clear that Afghanistan does not share borders with Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan.

s: Afghanistan does not have a common border with
